draft.personalized_opening: The announced Samfélag í bleyti pavilion treats bathing places as social infrastructure and names you as commissioner (https://www.honnunarmidstod.is/ha-frettir/samfelag-i-bleyti-er-framlag-islands-a-feneyjatviaeringi). draft.project_case: At a civic-building reception, I would compare a proxy handoff recess with a shared staffed waiting edge, while retaining direct personal entry. draft.personalized_ask: Could you advise which Icelandic architect or interactive-design researcher would best critique that civic tradeoff? I would value one precise introduction or a published reference before proposing a pilot.
draft.body:
Dear Halla Helgadóttir,

The announced Samfélag í bleyti pavilion treats bathing places as social infrastructure and names you as commissioner (https://www.honnunarmidstod.is/ha-frettir/samfelag-i-bleyti-er-framlag-islands-a-feneyjatviaeringi). Its emphasis on shared everyday life is relevant to the proposed study.

I’m developing Proxy Society, an architecture research project on AI agents and robots acting for absent people under limited, revocable mandates. At a civic-building reception, I would compare a proxy handoff recess with a shared staffed waiting edge, while retaining direct personal entry. The study would ask whether a delegated transaction saves time but removes an opportunity for encounter, and whether people can withdraw the instruction and stay.

Could you advise which Icelandic architect or interactive-design researcher would best critique that civic tradeoff? I would value one precise introduction or a published reference before proposing a pilot.

Best regards,
Kris Haamer

draft.body:
Dear Architects Association of Iceland team,

Your statement on public-building quality emphasizes how architecture connects people and neighborhoods (https://www.honnunarmidstod.is/ha-frettir/vondu%C3%B0-honnun-er-abyrg-uppbygging). I want to keep that effect visible when evaluating delegated access.

I’m developing Proxy Society, an architecture research project on AI agents and robots acting for absent people under limited, revocable mandates. At a civic room’s entrance, I would compare a common waiting bench with a separate proxy bay. An AI representative would request one booking under a mandate that expires or can be withdrawn. Plans and staged observation would test accessibility, encounters and human handoff, retaining a person’s own attendance.

Could you recommend a member with relevant civic-building experience who could critique this pilot, and advise how to approach an operator for an initial research discussion? No site access is assumed.

Best regards,
Kris Haamer
Proxy Society
https://proxysociety.org/architecture
